cards.explanation: The answer is that Solomon rebuilds the cities and settles Israelites there. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, rebuilds the cities Hiram had given him and settles Israelites there (2 Chronicles 8:2). Somebody handed him a fixer-upper and he went straight to work, friends. Me, I got handed a junk drawer once, and I spent my time welcoming the newcomers.
The answer is True. The text says Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and captured it (2 Chronicles 8:3). Short verse, big result, friends. Solomon goes, and the city is captured.

The answer is that Solomon makes them forced laborers. The text says Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day (2 Chronicles 8:8). These were descendants who remained in the land, and the Israelites had not destroyed them. It's a heavy part of the passage, friends, and I think it's worth slowing down on.

The answer is that the Israelites are his men of war and commanders. Solomon didn't consign any Israelites to slave labor, because they were his men of war, the leaders of his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry (2 Chronicles 8:9). Verse 10 adds that they were also his chief officers, 250 supervisors (2 Chronicles 8:10). I think that's a team nobody wanted to be late to a meeting with, friends.

The answer is that the places the ark has entered are holy. Solomon says, "My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy." (2 Chronicles 8:11) That's the reason the text gives, friends, and it's the one Solomon gives. So he moves her to the palace he built for her.

The answer is False. Solomon appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites "In keeping with the ordinances of his father David…" and the gatekeepers were set up because it had been the command of David, the man of God (2 Chronicles 8:14). So this wasn't a plan apart from David, friends. Solomon, David's son, was carrying out what his father commanded.

The answer is that the command is followed without turning aside in any matter. The text says they "…did not turn aside from the king’s command regarding the priests or the Levites in any matter, including that of the treasuries." (2 Chronicles 8:15) Any matter, friends, and that includes the treasuries. That's a crew that follows instructions.

The answer is True. The text says all the work of Solomon was carried out, from the day the foundation was laid for the house of the LORD until it was finished (2 Chronicles 8:16). So the house of the LORD was completed, friends. Start to finish, nothing left hanging.

The answer is Hiram, king of Tyre. Hiram sent Solomon ships captained by his servants, along with crews of experienced sailors (2 Chronicles 8:18). Hiram is king of Tyre (2 Chronicles 2:3), the same Hiram who gave Solomon those cities (2 Chronicles 8:2). Looks like he's a generous neighbor, friends.

The answer is gold. Hiram's sailors went to Ophir and acquired 450 talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon (2 Chronicles 8:18). A talent is a big weight, friends, so that's a LOT of gold. Hiram also sent crews of experienced sailors with those ships.
